learning_goal: State where the axillary artery begins and ends, divide it into three parts by pectoralis minor, name the one, two and three branches of each part, and say where the vessel can safely be tied.

topics: arterial supply of the upper limb
terms: first part of the axillary artery
second part of the axillary artery

outer border of the first rib
Screw The Lawyer Save A Patient

structures.label: Outer border of the 1st rib
terms: outer border of the first rib
lateral border of the first rib
structures.narration: The name changes here. Medial to this line the vessel is the subclavian artery; lateral to it, the axillary. Nothing about the vessel itself changes — only the name.

structures.label: Lower border of teres major
structures.narration: And it ends here. Below the lower border of teres major it is called the brachial artery. One vessel, three names, two landmarks.

structures.label: Pectoralis minor
structures.narration: Pectoralis minor crosses in front of the artery and is what divides it into three parts. It is the single most useful muscle in the axilla for the exam, because it also gives the surgeon the three levels of nodes.

structures.label: Subclavian artery
structures.narration: What the axillary artery is before it crosses the first rib.

structures.label: Brachial artery
structures.narration: What it becomes in the arm.

structures.label: 1st part — above pectoralis minor
terms: first part of the axillary artery
structures.narration: From the outer border of the first rib to the upper border of pectoralis minor. It is covered by the clavipectoral fascia and gives one branch.

structures.label: 2nd part — behind pectoralis minor
terms: second part of the axillary artery
structures.narration: The part lying behind the muscle. It gives two branches, and it is the part the three cords of the brachial plexus are named around.

structures.label: 3rd part — below pectoralis minor
terms: third part of the axillary artery
structures.narration: From the lower border of pectoralis minor to the lower border of teres major. It gives three branches and it is the longest and the most exposed part.

structures.label: Superior thoracic artery
structures.narration: The only branch of the first part. A small vessel to the first and second intercostal spaces.

structures.label: Thoracoacromial artery
structures.narration: A short trunk that pierces the clavipectoral fascia and at once breaks into four: acromial, clavicular, deltoid, pectoral. Remember them as ACDP.

structures.label: Lateral thoracic artery
structures.narration: Runs down the lateral chest wall along the lower border of pectoralis minor. In the woman it gives lateral mammary branches, so it is part of the blood supply of the breast.

structures.label: Subscapular artery
structures.narration: The largest branch. It divides into the circumflex scapular artery, which turns back through the triangular space onto the scapula, and the thoracodorsal artery, which goes on to latissimus dorsi.

structures.label: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
structures.narration: The smaller of the pair. It crosses in front of the surgical neck and sends an ascending branch up the intertubercular groove to the head of the humerus.

structures.label: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
structures.narration: The larger of the pair. It passes backwards through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve — which is why a fracture of the surgical neck can take out both together.

structures.label: Axillary vein
structures.narration: Always medial to the artery and always in front of it at the lower end. In the axilla the vein is what the surgeon meets first.

structures.label: Cords of the brachial plexus
structures.narration: Lateral, posterior and medial cords take their names from where they lie against the second part of this artery. If you can find the artery you can name every cord.

structures.label: Axillary sheath
structures.narration: A sleeve of prevertebral fascia wrapping the artery and the cords together — but not the vein. Local anaesthetic put inside it blocks the whole limb, and that is the anatomy behind an axillary block.

structures.label: Scapular anastomosis
structures.narration: Around the scapula the suprascapular and dorsal scapular arteries from the subclavian meet the circumflex scapular from the subscapular. That bypass is what allows the artery to be tied between the first rib and the subscapular branch and the limb to survive.

views.title: Where it starts and where it stops
views.narration: One continuous vessel runs from the aortic arch to the fingers and changes its name twice on the way. At the outer border of the first rib the subclavian becomes the axillary. At the lower border of teres major the axillary becomes the brachial. Those two landmarks are worth marks on their own.

views.title: Pectoralis minor cuts it in three
views.narration: Lay pectoralis minor across the artery. What is above the muscle is the first part, what is behind it is the second, what is below it is the third. Everything else in this topic hangs off that one muscle.

views.title: One, two, three
views.narration: The parts number their own branches: one, two, three. First part, superior thoracic. Second part, thoracoacromial and lateral thoracic. Third part, subscapular, anterior circumflex humeral, posterior circumflex humeral. In order: Screw The Lawyer Save A Patient.

views.title: What travels with it
views.narration: Peel the axillary sheath off and three things are inside it: the artery and the cords, wrapped together. The vein is outside the sheath, medial to the artery, and it is the structure at risk in a clearance. This arrangement is why one injection into the sheath anaesthetises the whole arm.

views.title: Where you may tie it
views.narration: Blood can reach the limb round the scapula without passing through the axilla. So the artery may be tied proximal to the origin of the subscapular artery and the collateral circulation will carry the limb. Tie it distal to that origin and you have cut off the bypass as well — that limb is in danger.

views.title: Two clinical branches
views.narration: Two branches come up again and again. The posterior circumflex humeral runs with the axillary nerve through the quadrangular space around the surgical neck of the humerus, so a fracture or a dislocation threatens both. The lateral thoracic supplies the lateral part of the breast, so it matters in breast surgery and in the blood supply questions that go with it.

gaps: Routed to its deferred diagram mode, not to 3D. The catalog has no axillary artery and none of its six branches — searching it for axillary, thoracoacromial, circumflex humeral and subscapular returns nothing. The nearest models are the subclavian artery and the subclavian vein, which are the proximal continuations, not this vessel. 3d_anatomy stays first in preferred_modes and is recorded in deferred_modes.

This scene is deliberately NOT a second 3D axilla scene. The existing 'Axillary vessels & lymph nodes' scene already shows the space of the axilla in 3D using the subclavian continuations and the four walls, and its own gaps record that the one-two-three branch rule 'is the most examinable fact in this entry and it currently has no picture'. This diagram is that picture. The two scenes are complementary: the 3D scene teaches the space, this one teaches the branching tree that has no models. Authoring a third 3D scene from the same handful of wall muscles would have duplicated the first without teaching anything new.

Status is 'planned', not 'ready'. Structures, six beats, ops and narration are all authored, but no artwork has been drawn for the SVG engine, so nothing renders today. Promote to 'ready' once the three-part artery with its six labelled branches exists as artwork and the engine can play the six beats.

The scapular anastomosis is drawn as a single labelled region rather than as its individual vessels. The suprascapular and dorsal scapular arteries have no models and no separate diagram regions here; naming them inside the anastomosis region keeps beat 5 about the principle of collateral flow rather than about a vessel list.

PEEL_LAYER in beat 4 is authored because the teaching move is to take the sheath off and see what is inside it. On a drawn diagram the engine will reveal the layer rather than remove geometry, which is the intended degradation.
The axillary sheath itself has no model in the catalog, as the axillary vessels scene also records. It exists here only as a diagram region.
